newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl promises help on Poland EU bid, flood relief.
newsitem.headline: Kohl promises help on Poland EU bid, flood relief.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl promised on Monday to support Poland's efforts to join the European Union as quickly as possible and said relations between Germany and Poland had not been better this century.

At a news conference with Poland's president and prime minister, Kohl also said Germany was making available emergency aid to help Poland cope with devastating floods that have killed 36 people in the last week.

"I believe I can say quite openly, without meaning to boast, that today's warm and friendly discussions show the relations between our two countries have never been better in this century," Kohl said.

Polish President Alexander Kwasniewski said the meeting in Bonn, the first of what promise to be regular consultations of government leaders based on the German-French model, marked the start of a closer friendship.
"This summit meeting has brought a new quality to our relationship," said Kwasniewski, who praised Kohl for his strong support for Poland's successful bid to be invited to join NATO.

"That Germany has provided support for the flood victims so quickly helps confirm the fact that, at this dramatic moment, we are not only neighbours and partners, but friends as well," Kwasniewski said.

Since the fall of communism in Poland in 1989 and German unification in 1990, the World War Two foes have worked hard to strengthen bilateral ties as well as links between the regions on either side of the border.
Eager to entrench political and economic stability east of its borders, Germany has championed Poland's drive to bind itself to western European structures.

Kohl, sitting between Kwasniewski and Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, said he expected the European Commission, the EU's executive body, to announce this week that Poland is suitable for EU membership.
The commission already agreed in principle last Thursday to recommend that membership talks be opened with Poland and four other east European candidates.
"We Germans are in favour of a speedy EU entry for Poland," Kohl said, although he did not specify a target date.
Poland is Germany's largest trading partner in central and eastern Europe with an annual two-way trade volume of 28.6 billion marks.
Germany is Poland's most important trading partner, accounting for one-third of Poland's external trade, and there are 6,000 German-Polish joint ventures.
Kwasniewski said that in 1995, Kohl had said Poland would be in the EU by 2000. He said he hoped the prognosis would prove correct or not far off the mark.
Kohl did not specify what sort of flood relief Germany would provide but said Bonn would do what it could.

"We Germans watched with empathy and sorrow the television reports of the floods in Poland that are worse than anything seen in several centuries," Kohl said. "Today we spoke about how Germany can help. And we will of course do everything we can."
Floods in southern Poland swept through dozens of towns and cities across thousands of square kilometres and killed at least 35 people.
The country is desperately trying to raise funds for reconstruction and is also appealing for emergency relief aid, particularly items in short supply such as water pumps.
